styleAnswer.evidence: The copier is a small grey-white box with a dark panel and a few buttons. The measured facts are 13 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage, and 97% near-neutral dark edge pixels. Tone count is in range of the hedge (9) and below the cheese stall (17) and well (20). The outline is the problem: it is almost colourless near-black, a uniform sticker-style line around the whole shape. The references use tinted dark tones instead (hedge 0%, stall 1%, well 33% neutral). Only about 3 lightness steps are visible on the body, which is shallow against the 5-6 steps in Beodeul materials. The body reads as mostly flat panels with few texture dots, grain or per-surface highlights. Overall it is cleanly drawn but flatter and more sticker-like than the references, so it does not pass.

The measured 13 visible tones per tile are in the range of the hedge (9) and the stall (17), but most of them come from the small control panel and outline pixels rather than from shaded material ramps. The body ramp has only about 3 steps against 5-6 in the references. 97% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a uniform near-black line, the sticker look; the references with tinted outlines (hedge 0%, stall 1%) are far from this. The exact 5x5 flat-fill measure is 0%, but that is because the object is small and the panel details break up the blocks, not because of real texture. A careful artist would not accept it next to the stall and well: the outline is near-black and the shading is shallow.
